races.title: State Assembly, District 12
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Eric Lucan
cands.bio: Marin County Supervisor for District 5, which covers most of Novato, and president of the Board for 2026. Before that he spent 11 years on the Novato City Council, serving three terms as mayor. Describes himself as a small business owner. Holds an M.B.A. from Georgia State University (2005).

endorsements.text: California Nurses Association and California Mountain Biking Coalition, as listed on Ballotpedia.
U.S. Sen. Adam Schiff, Rep. Jared Huffman, Assembly Speaker Robert Rivas and former U.S. Sen. Barbara Boxer, among others, are quoted endorsing him on his campaign site.
CCAH PAC endorsement, listed on his campaign site (September 8, 2026).
Marin Independent Journal editorial board recommended him for Assembly (May and September 2026), per headlines and teasers on his campaign site.

cands.gaps: His birthplace and the year he came to California were not found. His upbringing in Marin rests on a supporter's quote on his campaign site, not an independent source. His background as a business owner is not specified, and the nature of the business was not found. No stated positions or actions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth limits, H-1B, policing, guns, abortion or school choice were found, apart from a board statement on an ICE lockup. The news articles listed on his campaign site could only be seen as short teasers, so their contents are not reported. The campaign site's About page was cut off.

local.label: Roots 90: A supporter quoted on his campaign site says he grew up in Marin County and is raising a family there, and he reports 19 years in local office there; his birthplace is not stated in the pages reviewed.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: By his own account, 19 years in local elected office: 11 on the Novato City Council (three-time mayor) and four as Marin County Supervisor, now Board president. He also describes himself as a small business owner. He has no prior state legislative service.
qual.why: Long local elected service and business ownership put him in the middle-to-upper part of the middle band. He has not served in the state legislature or in a state-level law or budget career.
qual.label: Long local elected service and business ownership put him in the middle-to-upper part of the middle band. He has not served in the state legislature or in a state-level law or budget career.

workers-first.evidence: As Marin Board of Supervisors president, he is quoted saying the Board is committed to opposing unlawful removals, federal overreach and actions that undermine due process, in response to a proposed ICE lockup in the Bay Area. The quote appears as a teaser on his campaign site; the full article was not read.

prio.label: Matches 0 of 1 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 0 only promised (needs 2 to score)

roots.summary: A supporter quoted on his campaign site says he grew up in Marin County and is raising a family there, and he reports 19 years in local office there; his birthplace is not stated in the pages reviewed.

cands.name: Jackie Elward
cands.bio: Rohnert Park City Councilmember, elected in 2020 as the first Black woman on the council, and a former mayor. She is an educator and school instructional assistant, a labor organizer with CSEA Local 75, and an immigrant from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. She ran for State Senate District 3 in 2024.

endorsements.text: Endorsed by the California Federation of Labor Unions, AFL-CIO; the California Teachers Association; the California Nurses Association; SEIU California State Council; and the Working Families Party, among others.
Her own survey response lists endorsements from Congressmember Mike Thompson, former Congressmember Lynn Woolsey, State Treasurer Fiona Ma, and Sonoma County District Attorney Carla Rodriguez.

cands.gaps: We could not find the year she moved to the United States or to California. We found no stated positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, guns, H-1B or immigration enforcement, police pay, or school vouchers and charters. We found no independent reporting on her council actions, so those come from her own descriptions. We found no documented controversies or foreign ties. The campaign site's priorities page was cut off, so some of her stated positions are missing.

local.label: Roots 40: She was born and raised in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and her campaign says she came to the U.S. a few years after meeting her husband in 2001; she then lived in Marin and Sonoma counties, so she arrived as an adult roughly 10 to 25 years ago.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Rohnert Park City Council member since 2020 and a former mayor. She is a director of Sonoma Clean Power and of the Sonoma County Continuum of Care, a school instructional assistant, and a CSEA Local 75 site representative. She ran for State Senate in 2024.
qual.why: Local elected office including a term as mayor puts her in the middle band. She has no state-level legislative service and no listed career in law or budget policy.
qual.label: Local elected office including a term as mayor puts her in the middle band. She has no state-level legislative service and no listed career in law or budget policy.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: She says she was a leader in the campaign for Measure B in Rohnert Park, which set an urban growth boundary to prevent sprawl and protect open space and farmland, and says "We must push back on efforts to pave over agricultural land."

pro-life.evidence: Her campaign site lists "Protecting Healthcare & Reproductive Rights" among her priorities; the text of that section was not available.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 2 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised

roots.summary: She was born and raised in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and her campaign says she came to the U.S. a few years after meeting her husband in 2001; she then lived in Marin and Sonoma counties, so she arrived as an adult roughly 10 to 25 years ago.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Says she led the campaign for Rohnert Park's Measure B urban growth boundary to prevent sprawl and protect open space and farmland, and that "We must push back on efforts to pave over agricultural land." She also supports more affordable housing.
